name: Liability for the insurer
blurb: When an algorithm denies care, the claims that follow: bad faith, breach of contract, unfair business practice, and the errors and omissions and D&O exposure behind them.

points.desc: Each of the tracked health insurer cases pleads breach of contract and breach of the implied covenant of good faith, the bad faith claim, alongside unjust enrichment and state unfair practice statutes; none pleads that AI is unlawful in itself, only that it replaced the individual review the policy promised.
points.name: The pattern in the three cases

points.desc: An insurer's own errors and omissions and directors and officers cover respond to these claims; the underwriting question is whether the carrier can show clinician review on every denial and a documented governance program for its tools.
points.name: Where the insurance for the insurer sits

summary: When an algorithm denies care, the claims that follow: bad faith, breach of contract, unfair business practice, and the errors and omissions and D&O exposure behind them.
